newsitem.title: USA: Skydiver injured in televised leap from tower.
newsitem.headline: Skydiver injured in televised leap from tower.

text.p: A skydiver leaping off Seattle's landmark Space Needle in a televised stunt was injured Thursday when her parachute failed to open properly, officials said.

Jessica Kluetmeier, 29, of New York, suffered a fractured vertebra when she spiraled down into a hard feet-first landing after the parachute did not open fully, said a spokeswoman for the Space Needle Corp., which authorised the jump.

Kluetmeier was among four members of the World BASE Jump Federation who leapt 520 feet (156 metres) off the observation deck level of the Space Needle for a broadcast of "American Journal," a syndicated television show.
The jump also was televised live on local television, and Kluetmeier could be seen tumbling and then spiraling down for a hard landing on the grass.

"Her parachute didn't open up all of the way, and some of the ropes got a little tangled," said Stephanie McNear, marketing coordinator for the Space Needle. "She did everything she was supposed to do to recover."
Kluetmeier, who remained conscious and alert after she landed, was admitted to Harbourview Medical Centre where she was reported in satisfactory condition and was expected to make a full recovery.
"Her spinal cord was not damaged," hospital spokesman Larry Zalin said.

It was the first time since the 605-foot (182-metre) Space Needle was built for the 1962 World's Fair that officials had authorised a parachute jump. In 1975 two skydivers jumped without authorisation and were not injured.
